=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves attach at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced apart along the stem, not clustered at nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf has multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (leaflets arranged in pairs along rachis with one terminal leaflet; terminal leaflet visible in all images)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (each compound leaf has three pairs of leaflets plus one terminal leaflet, totaling 7; visible in all images)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets arranged in pairs along the rachis, with one terminal leaflet; visible in all images)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins smooth with no teeth or serrations; visible in all images)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadest near the middle and taper to both ends; visible in all images)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaflets taper to a sharp point; visible in all images)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaflets taper to a narrow base; visible in all images)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with secondary veins branching off perpendicularly; visible in all images)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and run parallel to each other, closely spaced; visible in all images)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surface is glossy and reflects light; visible in all images)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on leaf surface; visible in all images)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, connecting leaf to stem; visible in all images)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round and cylindrical in cross-section; visible in all images)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly thickened, typical of woody seedlings; visible in all images)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem; visible in all images)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stem is green near the apex, transitioning to brownish at the base; visible in all images)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels; visible in all images)
